messages:
Maya: Kicking off network bring-up smoke for atl-gpu-nova cluster. Focus: TGW peering, NAT egress, split-horizon DNS, route propagation. Following quick checklist, ping me for blockers.

Alex: Copy. TGW attachments created?

DeployBot: tgw-attach-abc123 created 1945678601 for VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d

Sam: ran `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d` — shows attached but state=available and route table doesn't have propagated route.

Li: saw same — TGW route table not propagating. Prob missing association/propagate flag when creating attachment.

Alex: quick check: `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filter Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=tgw-0abc` then `aws ec2 get-transit-gateway-route-table-propagations --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0xx`

Sam: output: no propagations for attachment-id tgw-attach-abc123. Should be auto but our terraform omitted the propagate=true param.

Maya: ok make a manual propagate change and add route to TGW route table as temporary fix. Command:
```
aws ec2 enable-transit-gateway-route-table-propagation \
  --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0xx \
  --transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-abc123
```

Sam: ran enable-propagation, propagation shows pending -> available. Verified route appears in tgw-rtb.

Alex: next, VPC route table needs route -> transit-gateway. Add via:
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0aa --destination-cidr-block 10.42.0.0/16 --transit-gateway-id tgw-0abc
```

Li: did that, BGP/no BGP here but traffic flows to TGW. Confirmed `ip route` on bastion shows 10.42.0.0 via local.

Maya: DNS: we need split-horizon internal zone redwood-internal.atl. Does route53 private hosted zone exist and associate with new VPC?

Sam: private zone exists in us-east-1 zone Z12345. Associated to vpc-0a1b2c3d not yet. Command:
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d
```

Sam: associated. Ran `dig service.internal.redwood-internal.atl +short` -> returns 10.42.2.5

Alex: NAT/egress: observed egress through nat-3 with EIP eipalloc-0cde. Throughput spike ~400 Mbps during image pulls. We need to decide: single NAT gateway vs proxy egress pool.

Li: cost note: NAT data transfer for 400 Mbps 24h is ~$X/day — we should route large pulls to internal artifact mirror or use dedicated NAT fleet with 10G proxies.

Maya: action: enable caching proxy on cluster nodes for large image pulls and open ticket to infra for shared egress pool. Ticket: INFRA-2987

Sam: also found ephemeral EIP exhaustion risk — autoscaling NAT gateways won't scale EIPs fast. For now we attach Elastic IP per NAT; long term use AWS NAT Gateway + prefix delegation or use NAT instances behind NLB.

Alex: for immediate handoff: Maya to document steps and add to runbook, Li will validate TGW propagate fix, Sam will verify DNS & egress, I'll prepare handoff notes for oncall.

Maya: creating checklist and PR to terraform to add propagate=true and host zone association. Will also add cost estimate and mitigation (artifact mirror + registry caching). Assigning to Li for post-handoff validation.

oncall-bot: Assigned oncall to Li for the next 6 hours

Li: will run smoke script `scripts/network-smoke.sh atl-gpu-nova` and post results. Quick snippet:
```
# smoke checks
curl -fsS http://metadata.internal/health || echo "metadata fail"
dig +short service.internal.redwood-internal.atl | grep 10.42.2.5
nc -zv 10.42.2.5 6443
```

Sam: smoke passed except image pull latency on mirror. Opening INFRA-2990 for registry mirror config.

Maya: thanks everyone. Handoff doc link: /docs/runbooks/atl-gpu-nova-networking.md — I'll PR before EOD. :thumbsup:

Alex: :thumbsup:

Sam: :rocket:
